Write a concrete EXECUTION PLAN for "Fire Sprinkler Inspection App" built around the RED-TEAMED reality (not the optimistic pitch). Founder: Hooman ($25-150K; ~10-20 hrs/wk; wants $5-30K/mo; NOT his domain). Red-team findings (JSON): {
  "name": "Fire Sprinkler Inspection App",
  "slug": "fire_sprinkler",
  "assumptions_checked": [
    {
      "claim": "AI Vision + Fire-Specific quadrant is EMPTY / zero competition (the load-bearing premise of the 6.70)",
      "status": "FALSE",
      "evidence": "Inspect Point (15,000+ users, 4.5M inspections) ships NFPA-25 forms + photo/deficiency capture + branded 'Inspection Assistant' AI; ServiceTrade (1,300+ customers incl. Pye-Barker) ships NFPA-25 digital forms + photo/video deficiency docs + Stella AI; BuildingReports has 13M+ inspections / 1.5M buildings / 1,300+ companies with mobile barcode+photo; OxMaint markets AI visual inspection for fire systems; FireDesign.ai does AI sprinkler layout; NFPA itself runs AI sprinkler-placement projects. Mature, crowded FSM niche, not an empty lane (vendor sites, fetched 2026-07-02)."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Pure SW, ~$0 hardware, runs on existing iPads, founder can build himself",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "No hardware and runs on owned iPads, but the doc's own BOM is $200-225K and lists TWO mandatory hires (iOS dev + licensed fire-protection PE/NICET-IV domain expert). Founder lacks both. Not a solo nights/weekends build; $0 refers only to the hardware line."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Regulatory driver: NFPA 25 mandate creates inelastic demand for the app",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "NFPA 25 mandates annual ITM (real, inelastic) but that demand is already fully served by paper, Excel, and incumbents. The mandate drives demand for the inspection, not for this app; and liability from regulated reports makes buyers MORE wary of unproven outsider AI, not less."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Proprietary training-data / network-effect moat accrues to the founder",
      "status": "FALSE",
      "evidence": "The corpus is already owned by incumbents (Inspect Point 4.5M inspections, BuildingReports 13M+). Founder faces the doc's own Gate-1 cold-start: needs 1,000+ labeled deficiency images that 'do not exist publicly' and can only come from customers he can't reach. Moat is inverted and belongs to incumbents."
    },
    {
      "claim": "WTP supports $199-399 per seat/month (Year-1 $1.79M ARR)",
      "status": "FALSE",
      "evidence": "Verified market seat pricing: ServiceTrade ~$75/tech/mo (office users free); FireLab ~$299/mo FLAT for unlimited technicians; general fire-inspection SW $29-$700/mo. Pitch prices a single bolt-on AI feature at 3-5x a full platform seat; realistic WTP for the add-on is ~$0-30/seat. Revenue math off ~1000x."
    },
    {
      "claim": "Buyer is reachable / sales are reasonably fast",
      "status": "FALSE",
      "evidence": "Doc concedes conservative relationship-driven trade, 3-6mo sales cycles, 40-60% still on paper, 'trust earned at trade shows,' negative signal 'we'd need it to be perfect.' Founder has zero industry connections and no domain credibility; multi-quarter high-touch grind in his documented distribution weakness."
    },
    {
      "claim": "AI-safe secondary income",
      "status": "PARTIALLY-TRUE",
      "evidence": "Regulated-workflow/liability/trade-trust layer is somewhat AI-safe, but the core camera-identifies-head-flags-deficiency task is increasingly zero-shot for general multimodal models, and NFPA + incumbents are already shipping AI; defensible layer (domain credibility + labeled corpus) is exactly what the founder lacks and incumbents own."
    }
  ],
  "competitors": [
    "Inspect Point — cloud fire-protection ITM platform, 15,000+ users, 4.5M inspections, 20M assets, $100M invoices, $28M raised (Mainsail 2022); NFPA-25 forms + photo/deficiency capture + 'Inspection Assistant' AI; demo-only pricing",
    "ServiceTrade — FSM for fire/mechanical, 1,300+ customers incl. Pye-Barker & Guardian; NFPA-25 digital forms + photo/video deficiency docs + Stella AI; ~$75/technician/month, office users free",
    "BuildingReports — 13M+ inspections, 1.5M buildings, 650M devices, 1,300+ inspection companies; ScanSeries mobile barcode+photo, NFPA/state/federal formats; demo-only pricing",
    "FireLab — cloud fire inspection (alarm+), iOS/Android/Windows; ~$299/month FLAT for unlimited technicians",
    "InspectNTrack — barcode-driven fire life-safety inspection/tracking; demo-only",
    "BuildOps — commercial-contractor platform, $127M+ raised, $1B+ valuation, 1,500+ contractors, OpsAI (fire is one of 6 verticals)",
    "OxMaint — CMMS marketing AI-powered visual inspection for fire systems",
    "FireDesign.ai — AI sprinkler layout + hydraulic calc from DXF/DWG (design side)",
    "SafetyCulture (iAuditor) — $2B+ general inspection platform, configurable for fire",
    "NFPA (standards body) — running its own AI projects for sprinkler placement / ceiling-height estimation"
  ],
  "honest_economics": "Cash to a credible MVP is $200-225K (doc's own BOM: 6-mo runway + mandatory iOS-dev hire + domain-expert contract) — at/over the founder's $25-150K ceiling and requiring two hires for skills he lacks; NOT a nights/weekends build. Year-1 net ~$0 (likely negative after the spend). Base case at 24 months, IF it survives the cold-start data wall and lands a few small shops at a realistic $50-80/seat (not $199-399): ~$1-4K/mo gross → ~$0-2K/mo net after hosting, ongoing domain-expert retainer, and his time. Low-probability upside (survives, ~50-100 seats): $3-6K/mo gross — but Inspect Point can ship the same CV feature to its 15K users faster than a non-domain solo can reach 100 seats. vs. the pitch's $1.79M ARR yr1 / $5.4M yr2, off by ~1000x (same gross-as-profit + top-decile-as-base-case pattern that cut CutLog and Track-B).",
  "hrs_per_week": "Not passive. 15-25 hrs/wk for the first 6-12 months (managing an iOS contractor + a domain expert, cold outreach, trade-show relationship building, data-collection partnerships), then 10-15 hrs/wk ongoing trust-based sales/support — lands in the same evening focus hours CutLog needs and routes into his weakest muscle (distribution/domain trust).",
  "kill_risks": [
    "'Empty quadrant / zero competition' is FALSE — Inspect Point (15K users, 4.5M inspections), ServiceTrade (1,300+ customers), and BuildingReports (13M+ inspections) already own the platform, the NFPA-25 workflow, the photo/deficiency capture, the proprietary labeled corpus, AND branded AI. A CV head-recognizer is a copyable feature, not a product.",
    "Seat price is fiction: market is $0 office-users / ~$75 per tech (ServiceTrade) or $299/mo flat for a whole team (FireLab); WTP for a bolt-on recognizer is a small fraction of the assumed $199-399/seat. Revenue math off ~1000x.",
    "Founder-fit inverted + two mandatory hires — non-domain, no iOS, no trade network; the hard non-delegable work (domain credibility, trade trust, distribution) is exactly his weakness. $200K+ and >15 hrs/wk, not a solo build.",
    "Cold-start data wall — needs proprietary labeled deficiency photos he can only get from the conservative customers he can't reach; the doc's own Gate-1 kill risk is likely to trigger.",
    "Conservative, liability-sensitive, slow-adopting buyer — 3-6mo trust-based sales cycles; NFPA mandate makes buyers warier of unproven outsider AI, not more eager."
  ],
  "revised_score": 3.6,
  "verdict": "PASS",
  "confidence": "MEDIUM",
  "_t": {
    "slug": "fire_sprinkler",
    "name": "Fire Sprinkler Inspection App",
    "read": "/home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/deep_research/sprinkler_inspection/ and its row in /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/deep_research/MASTER_COMPARISON.md (optimistic 6.70).",
    "claims": "Pure SW, ~$0 hardware, regulatory driver (NFPA 25 mandates inspections), data moat, 15K+ fire-protection firms, runs on existing iPads. RED-TEAM SKEPTICALLY: who already ships fire-inspection software (BuildingReports, Inspect Point, ServiceTrade, InspectNTrack, JLL/Building Engines, FireLab, TapReports, Joyfill)? Is this a saturated field-service-management niche? What is real WTP vs incumbents; switching costs; is the \"data moat\" real? Is the buyer reachable/fast, or a conservative slow-adopting trade? Gross vs net, realistic ramp, honest hrs/wk for a solo non-domain founder."
  }
}
Also read /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/trackA_redteam/fire_sprinkler/01_redteam.md.

If the red-team verdict is PASS, still write the plan BUT lead with the honest "why this is likely not worth it" and what would have to be true to change that. Plan must cover: the specific target segment/wedge, first 90 days week-by-week, path to revenue + realistic ramp, itemized budget within $25-150K, delegation to keep it part-time, go/no-go gates, and cheapest validation before spending real money.
WRITE to /home/colligo/hs_scripts/claude/auto_research/runs/trackA_redteam/fire_sprinkler/02_execution_plan.md (use Write). Return a ~180-word summary and pass along the slug.

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). 1	# Red-Team: Fire Sprinkler Inspection App
2	
3	**Created**: 2026-07-02 by Claude (Opus 4.8, adversarial red-team). **Owner**: Hooman Shariati.
4	**Standard applied**: same rigor that cut CutLog 8.85 → 4.5 and busted the Track-B batch
5	(`runs/FLAT_SHOWDOWN.md`, `runs/trackB/DEEP_DIVE_SYNTHESIS.md`).
6	**Optimistic source under review**: `runs/cycle_015/step5_execution/deep_research/*` — scored **6.70 CONDITIONAL-GO**.
7	
8	**Founder**: Adobe eng manager; AI/ML + cloud + infra; EE; mech-eng friends; $25–150K capital;
9	~10–20 hrs/wk; wants $5–30K/mo secondary income; AI-safe preferred. **NOT his domain** (zero
10	fire-protection knowledge, self-admitted 6/10 fit, no iOS experience).
11	
12	---
13	
14	## TL;DR
15	
16	The 6.70 rests on one load-bearing claim: **"the AI Vision + Fire-Specific quadrant is EMPTY —
17	no competition."** That claim is **FALSE**. This is a mature, crowded field-service-management
18	(FSM) niche where the entrenched incumbents already ship the entire workflow (scheduling →
19	NFPA-25 digital forms → photo/deficiency capture → auto report → invoicing), already have
20	15,000+ users and 13M+ inspections of proprietary data, already brand AI features, and already
21	price at **1/3 to 1/5 of what this pitch assumes**. The founder is a non-domain outsider selling
22	a *point feature* (head recognition) into a *whole-platform* purchase decision, to a conservative
23	trade, with no distribution and a training-data cold-start he can't solve without the very
24	customers he can't reach. **Revised score: 3.6/10, PASS.**
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 1. Claim-by-claim autopsy
29	
30	### Claim A: "AI Vision + Fire-Specific quadrant is EMPTY / zero competition" — **FALSE**
31	
32	This is the single premise the whole 6.70 stands on (drives Moat 8, Tech Risk 7, the entire
33	GO verdict). Real market:
34	
35	| Incumbent | Scale (sourced) | NFPA-25 forms | Photo / deficiency capture | AI branded | Pricing |
36	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
37	| **Inspect Point** | **15,000+ users**, 4.5M inspections, 20M assets, $100M invoices [inspectpoint.com] | Yes (NFPA, ULC, Joint Commission, CA Title 19, hundreds of jurisdictional forms) | **Yes — "deficiency details complete with notes and photos"** | **Yes — "Inspection Assistant," "tools tailored for fire protection—powered by AI," catches missing/inaccurate fields** | demo-only |
38	| **ServiceTrade** | **1,300+ customers** incl. Pye-Barker, Guardian [servicetrade.com] | Yes ("NFPA 25-compliant digital inspection forms") | **Yes — documents issues with photos and videos** | **Yes — Stella AI assistants + Smart Insights** | **~$75/tech/mo, office users free** |
39	| **BuildingReports** | **13M+ inspections, 1.5M buildings, 650M devices, 1,300+ inspection companies** [buildingreports.com] | "From NFPA to State and Federal formats" | **Yes — ScanSeries mobile app, barcode + photo** | Not yet | demo-only |
40	| **FireLab** | Cloud fire inspection (alarm+), iOS/Android/Windows | Yes | Yes | — | **~$299/mo flat, unlimited technicians** |
41	| **InspectNTrack** | Barcode-driven inspection/tracking | Yes (fire life-safety) | Yes | — | demo-only |
42	| **OxMaint** | CMMS | Fire systems | Yes | **"AI-powered visual inspection … analyzes inspection data to detect failures early"** | — |
43	| **FireDesign.ai** | Startup | — (design side) | — | **AI sprinkler layout + hydraulic from DXF/DWG** | — |
44	| **NFPA (the standards body itself)** | — | — | — | **Documented AI projects for ceiling-height + optimal sprinkler placement** | — |
45	
46	**Verdict**: the "empty quadrant" is a mapping artifact. The deep-research doc defined the axis
47	so narrowly ("photo-based *deficiency* CV specifically") that it declared victory in a lane that
48	exists only on its own diagram. The buyer does not buy a quadrant; the buyer buys a platform, and
49	every platform already does NFPA-25 forms + photo-tagged deficiencies + a report at the click of a
50	button + branded AI. Adding a CNN that guesses "pendent vs. upright" is a **feature**, not a
51	product — and it's a feature the 15K-user incumbent with 4.5M inspections of labeled photos is far
52	better positioned to ship than a solo outsider. This is the identical failure mode that busted
53	CutLog ("zero competition" → live free clone + OEM tables) and the Track-B batch ("under-served"
54	bookkeeping → Kruze/Zeni/Pilot already own it).
55	
56	### Claim B: "Pure SW, ~$0 hardware, runs on existing iPads" — **PARTIALLY-TRUE**
57	
58	True that there's no hardware and it runs on iPads the trade already owns. But the doc's own
59	feasibility BOM is **$200–225K** (6-month build + a **hired iOS dev** + a **contracted licensed
60	fire-protection PE/NICET-IV domain expert** — both flagged as mandatory GO conditions). So "$0"
61	is the *hardware* line only; the real cash-to-MVP is $200K+ and, more importantly, **it requires
62	hiring for two of the three core competencies the founder lacks (domain + iOS).** That is not a
63	"pure software play he can build himself" — it's a two-hire venture. Founder-fit is inverted the
64	same way CutLog's was: his genuine edge (CV modeling) is the *easy, commoditized* part; the hard,
65	non-delegable parts (domain credibility, trade relationships, iOS field UX) are his weaknesses.
66	
67	### Claim C: "Regulatory driver — NFPA 25 mandates inspections → inelastic demand" — **PARTIALLY-TRUE but misread**
68	
69	NFPA 25 does mandate annual ITM, and that demand is real and inelastic. **But the mandate creates
70	demand for the inspection, not for THIS app.** The mandate is *already* fully served by paper,
71	Excel, and the incumbents above. A regulatory mandate to *do* inspections is not a wedge unless
72	you're the cheapest/only way to comply — and you're neither. Worse: because reports carry
73	**liability** (a missed deficiency can void insurance), the regulated nature makes buyers *more*
74	conservative about trusting an unproven AI from a no-name outsider, not less. The mandate is a
75	tailwind for the incumbents' renewals, not a crowbar for a new entrant.
76	
77	### Claim D: "Data moat / network effect — every inspection makes the model better" — **FALSE (inverted)**
78	
79	The moat is real but it belongs to **Inspect Point and BuildingReports**, not to the founder.
80	They already hold the proprietary labeled-photo corpus (4.5M and 13M+ inspections respectively).
81	The founder faces the exact cold-start the doc itself flags as Gate-1 kill risk: he needs 1,000+
82	labeled deficiency images that "do not exist publicly anywhere," which he can only get from fire
83	companies who won't share proprietary photos with an outsider before the product exists. So the
84	"moat" is (a) already owned by incumbents and (b) a chicken-and-egg wall for him. Same pattern as
85	CutLog: the network already exists and someone else built it.
86	
87	### Claim E: "15K+ firms, real TAM" — **PARTIALLY-TRUE but the SAM is tiny and the seat price is fiction**
88	
89	15K firms / ~50K inspectors is real. But the doc's own Market score is 5/10 and admits a
90	**$30–50M realistically addressable** ceiling. The revenue math ($199–399 **per seat/month**) is
91	where it collapses: verified market seat pricing is **ServiceTrade ~$75/tech/mo (office free)** and
92	**FireLab ~$299/mo flat for the whole team**; general fire-inspection software runs **$29–$700/mo**
93	[softwareadvice/getapp-class sources; DDG pricing digest]. This pitch prices a *single AI feature*
94	at **3–5× the price of a full incumbent platform seat**, and higher than FireLab charges an entire
95	company. WTP for a bolt-on recognizer, on top of the platform they already pay for, is a small
96	fraction of $299 — realistically $0–30/seat, if they don't just wait for Inspect Point to ship it
97	free in the next release. The Year-1 "$1.79M ARR / 500 seats" is a top-decile fantasy layered on a
98	mispriced seat.
99	
100	### Claim F: "Buyer reachable / fast" — **FALSE**
101	
102	Fire protection is a **conservative, relationship-driven, slow-adopting trade** (the doc's own
103	Accessibility 6 and "3–6 month sales cycles," "40–60% still on paper," "trust earned at trade shows"
104	concede this). The founder has **zero industry connections**, no domain credibility, and lives in
105	AI-platform/Firefly land, not NFSA chapter meetings. Selling liability-bearing AI to skeptical
106	inspectors who "won't trust it until it's perfect" (a listed negative signal) is a multi-quarter,
107	in-person, high-touch grind — the antithesis of a 10–20 hr/wk secondary stream, and squarely in his
108	documented distribution weakness.
109	
110	### Claim G: "AI-safe" — **PARTIALLY-TRUE, degrading**
111	
112	Regulated-workflow + liability + trade trust is *somewhat* AI-safe. But the core "point a camera,
113	identify the head, flag paint/corrosion" task is exactly what a general multimodal model (GPT-5-class
114	vision, Gemini) can increasingly do zero-shot, and NFPA + incumbents are already building AI in. The
115	defensible layer is domain credibility and the labeled corpus — both of which the founder lacks and
116	incumbents own.
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 2. Honest economics (re-derived, solo non-domain founder)
121	
122	**Cash to a credible MVP**: $200–225K (doc's own BOM: 6-mo runway + iOS hire + domain-expert
123	contract). This *exceeds* the founder's stated $25–150K envelope at the top end and requires hiring
124	for skills he lacks. It is **not** a nights-and-weekends build like CutLog.
125	
126	**Revenue reality**:
127	- Real market seat value for a *bolt-on AI feature* against free/$75 incumbents: **$0–30/seat/mo**,
128	  not $199–399.
129	- Realistic reachable customers in Year 1 for a non-domain solo with no distribution: **single-digit
130	  to low-double-digit seats**, gated by 3–6 month trust-building sales cycles.
131	- **Honest Year-1 net: ~$0** (likely negative after the $200K+ spend). Base-case at 24 months, *if*
132	  it survives cold-start and lands a few small shops: **$1–4K/mo gross → ~$0–2K/mo net** after
133	  hosting, the domain-expert retainer needed to keep NFPA logic current, and his own time.
134	- Upside case (survives, prices at a realistic $50–80/seat, reaches ~50–100 seats): **$3–6K/mo gross**
135	  — but that requires beating or partnering with Inspect Point, and Inspect Point can ship the same
136	  CV feature to its 15K users faster than he can reach 100. Probability of the upside: low.
137	
138	vs. the pitch's **$1.79M ARR Year 1 / $5.4M Year 2** — off by ~1000×, the same
139	gross-read-as-profit + top-decile-as-base-case pattern that cut CutLog and Track-B.
140	
141	**Weekly time load**: NOT passive. 15–25 hrs/wk for the first 6–12 months (managing an iOS
142	contractor, managing a domain expert, cold outreach + trade-show relationship building + data-
143	collection partnerships), then 10–15 hrs/wk ongoing sales/support in a trade that buys on trust.

# Execution Plan: Fire Sprinkler Inspection App

**Created**: 2026-07-02 by Claude (Opus 4.8). **Owner**: Hooman Shariati.
**Inputs**: `01_redteam.md` (revised score **3.6/10, PASS, MEDIUM confidence**),
`deep_research/sprinkler_inspection/`, `MASTER_COMPARISON.md` (optimistic 6.70).
**Founder**: Adobe eng mgr; AI/ML + cloud + EE; $25–150K capital; ~10–20 hrs/wk;
wants $5–30K/mo; AI-safe preferred. **NOT his domain** (zero fire-protection knowledge,
no iOS, no trade network).

---

## 0. LEAD: Why this is likely NOT worth building (read this first)

The red-team verdict is **PASS**. This plan exists so the decision is made on evidence, not
on skipping the work. Bottom line up front: **do not build this as a startup.** Five reasons,
each independently fatal:

1. **The "empty quadrant" is false.** Inspect Point (15K users, 4.5M inspections), ServiceTrade
   (1,300+ customers, Stella AI), and BuildingReports (13M+ inspections) already ship the whole
   workflow — NFPA-25 forms, photo/deficiency capture, auto-report, AND branded AI. A CV
   head-recognizer is a **feature they can copy**, not a product you can defend.
2. **The data moat is inverted.** The proprietary labeled-photo corpus is already owned by the
   incumbents. You start at a cold-start wall — you need ~1,000+ labeled deficiency images that
   don't exist publicly and can only come from the conservative customers you can't reach.
3. **The seat price is fiction.** Market reality: ServiceTrade ~$75/tech/mo (office users free),
   FireLab ~$299/mo FLAT for a whole team. The pitch's $199–399/seat for a single bolt-on feature
   is 3–5× a full platform seat. Real WTP for the add-on: ~$0–30/seat. Revenue math off ~1000×.
4. **Founder-fit is inverted + it needs two hires.** Your genuine edge (CV modeling) is the
   commoditized part. The hard, non-delegable parts — domain credibility, trade trust, distribution,
   iOS field UX — are exactly your weaknesses. Real cash-to-MVP is $200–225K (over your ceiling)
   and requires hiring an iOS dev and a licensed fire-protection PE/NICET-IV expert.
5. **The buyer is slow and liability-averse.** 3–6mo trust-based sales cycles, 40–60% still on
   paper, "trust earned at trade shows." NFPA mandate makes them *warier* of unproven outsider AI,
   not more eager. This routes straight into your weakest muscle and consumes your scarcest hours.

**Honest economics**: Year-1 net ~$0 (negative after spend). 24-month base case if it survives:
$1–4K/mo gross → $0–2K/mo net. Low-prob upside: $3–6K/mo — but Inspect Point ships the same CV
feature to 15K users faster than a non-domain solo reaches 100 seats. This ranks **below CutLog
(4.5)** and **below buy-a-micro-SaaS (5.2)**.

### What would have to be TRUE to change the verdict

Only build if you can prove ALL of these BEFORE spending real money (see §7 validation):

- **T1 — A reachable co-founder/partner supplies domain + distribution.** A licensed
  fire-protection PE / NICET-IV inspector or a small-shop owner who becomes an equity partner (not
  a paid contractor), bringing the trade network and the labeled photos. Without this the moat and
  the distribution are both unsolved.
- **T2 — An incumbent wants to buy/license the CV module, not compete with it.** If Inspect Point
  or ServiceTrade signals real interest in a white-label CV deficiency-detector, this becomes a BD
  play (§6, Plan B) with a built-in data source and distribution — the only non-suicidal shape.
- **T3 — Real WTP for the standalone add-on is >$40/seat AND ≥5 shops will pre-pay.** Verified via
  paid LOIs, not verbal interest, from shops the incumbents *don't* already serve.
- **T4 — A defensible wedge exists that general multimodal models can't do zero-shot.** The core
  "identify head / flag corrosion" task is increasingly free from GPT-5-class/Gemini vision. You
  need a task that requires proprietary structured NFPA-25 logic + labeled edge cases, not a CNN.

If you cannot demonstrate T1–T4 in the ~$2–5K validation phase below, **stop**. The rest of this
plan is the disciplined path to test those cheaply and kill fast — it is NOT a green light to build.

---

## 1. IF you proceed anyway: the ONLY viable target segment / wedge

Do **not** attempt to build a competing platform. The only shape with any chance:

- **Wedge**: a **narrow, standalone CV "second-set-of-eyes" deficiency checker** that sits
  *alongside* whatever platform a shop already uses — not a replacement. It ingests photos the
  inspector already takes and flags likely NFPA-25 deficiencies (paint/corrosion, obstruction,
  wrong head type, missing escutcheon) as a QA/liability-reduction layer.
- **Target segment**: **small independent fire-protection shops (2–15 inspectors)** that are
  *still on paper/Excel* (the 40–60%) and are NOT customers of Inspect Point/ServiceTrade — i.e.
  the sliver the incumbents haven't captured. These shops have real liability pain and no AI.
- **Buyer**: owner-operator (not enterprise procurement). One person decides.
- **Positioning**: "cut your callback/liability risk" (a cost story on their next invoice), NOT
  "AI platform." Frame as insurance against a missed deficiency voiding a client's coverage.
- **Explicitly out of scope**: alarms, hydraulic design, scheduling, invoicing, multi-vertical.
  The moment you add these you are rebuilding the incumbent platform with none of their advantages.

Reality check: even this wedge is a hard sell and a small TAM. It exists here only because it's the
single configuration that doesn't require out-executing a $28M-funded 15K-user incumbent head-on.

---

## 2. First 90 days — week-by-week (validation-first, near-zero spend)

The first 90 days spend **~$2–5K total** and are designed to hit the T1–T4 go/no-go gates BEFORE
any hire or build. If any gate fails, you stop and keep the rest of the budget.

**Weeks 1–2 — Landscape + kill-check the premise yourself.**
- Demo/trial Inspect Point, ServiceTrade, FireLab, BuildingReports ScanSeries. Confirm exactly what
  their photo/deficiency + AI already do. Document the real feature gap (likely small).
- Read NFPA-25 ITM basics + 3–5 recent fire-inspection Reddit/Facebook threads. Cost: ~$0.

**Weeks 3–4 — Find the domain partner (T1). This is the real gate.**
- Post in fire-protection Facebook groups, r/fir eprotection, NFSA/AFSA chapter lists. Cold-DM 30
  small-shop owners and independent NICET-IV inspectors. Goal: 5 discovery calls. Offer nothing but
  a conversation about their liability/callback pain. Cost: ~$0.
- If NO credible domain person will even talk to you → **GATE G1 FAIL, stop.**

**Weeks 5–6 — Pain + WTP interviews (T3).**
- Run 8–12 structured calls with small-shop owners. Ask: how do you catch missed deficiencies today?
  What does a callback/liability incident cost you? Would you pay for a photo QA checker, and how much?
- Do NOT pitch. Listen for whether the pain is top-3 and unaddressed. Cost: ~$0.

**Weeks 7–8 — Zero-shot feasibility spike (T4). Plays to your actual strength.**
- Take 50–100 real deficiency photos (from partner or public sources) and test GPT-5-class + Gemini
  vision zero-shot vs. a light fine-tune. Measure accuracy on head-type ID + top deficiency classes.
- If general models already do this ~well zero-shot → your CV "moat" is gone → **GATE G4 FAIL, stop**
  (or pivot to pure NFPA-25 structured-logic layer). Cost: ~$200–500 API + your time.

**Weeks 9–10 — Fake-door / paid-LOI test (T3 hard proof).**
- Build a one-page landing + a Figma/clickable mock (no real app). Run $500–1,000 of targeted ads +
  partner referrals. Ask for a refundable $50–100 pre-order deposit or signed pilot LOI.
- Target: **≥5 shops put money/signature down.** Verbal "sounds cool" does not count. Cost: ~$1–2K.

**Weeks 11–12 — Incumbent-interest probe (T2) + decision.**
- Email BD contacts at Inspect Point / ServiceTrade proposing a licensed CV module. Gauge buy/partner
  interest (this is Plan B and often the better outcome).
- **Compile go/no-go against §5 gates. Default action is STOP unless every gate is green.** Cost: ~$0.

Total 90-day spend: **~$2–5K.** No hires, no app build, no long-term commitment until gates pass.

---

## 3. Path to revenue + realistic ramp

Only relevant if gates pass (low probability). Ordered by realism:

- **Fastest cash (Plan B, preferred)**: license/BD the CV module to an incumbent. One deal could
  return more than years of solo seat-selling and solves data + distribution. Ramp: 2–4 quarters of
  BD; outcome binary. This is a services/BD income, not a startup.
- **Direct wedge (Plan A)**: pilot 3–5 small shops → convert to paid at a **realistic $40–80/seat/mo**
  (NOT $199–399). Ramp: months 4–9 = 3–5 pilots (mostly free/discounted for data); months 9–18 =
  first paying shops; 24-month base case **~10–40 seats → $1–4K/mo gross → $0–2K/mo net.** Upside
  (unlikely): 50–100 seats → $3–6K/mo gross.
- **This does NOT reach the $5–30K/mo target on any realistic path.** Say so out loud in the go/no-go.

---

## 4. Itemized budget (within $25–150K; staged, gated)

Budget is released **in stages tied to gates** — you never spend the build tranche unless validation
passes. Total exposure if you stop at validation: **~$5K.**

| Stage | Item | Cost | Released when |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0 Validation** | Competitor trials, incidentals | $0–300 | now |
| | Zero-shot vision API spend (spike) | $200–500 | wk 7 |
| | Landing page + Figma mock + tools | $200–500 | wk 9 |
| | Fake-door ad spend | $1,000–2,000 | wk 9 |
| | **Validation subtotal** | **~$2–5K** | — |
| **1 Design partner** | Domain expert (NICET-IV) — **equity/rev-share, not salary** if possible; else short paid scoping | $0–5K | only if G1+G3 pass |
| **2 MVP (only if all gates pass)** | iOS/mobile contractor (thin PWA first, not native) | $30–60K | only if paid LOIs in hand |
| | Backend + CV pipeline (you build) | ~$0 (your time) + $2–5K infra/API | with Stage 2 |
| | Domain-expert retainer (keep NFPA logic current) | $1–2K/mo | ongoing |
| | **Build subtotal** | **~$40–75K** | gated |

Notes: (a) Prefer a **PWA over native iOS** to avoid the mandatory iOS hire and cut cost — iPads run
web fine. (b) Prefer an **equity/rev-share domain partner** over a paid contractor — it also solves
distribution and data (T1). (c) Keep total exposure under ~$75K even in the build case; do NOT hit
the $200K+ figure the optimistic BOM implied.

---

## 5. Go / No-Go gates (default = NO-GO)

| Gate | Week | Pass condition | On fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G1 Domain partner** | 4 | A credible NICET-IV/shop-owner will partner (equity or committed pilot) | STOP |
| **G2 Pain is top-3** | 6 | ≥6/10 interviewed owners name missed-deficiency/liability as a real recurring cost | STOP |
| **G3 Paid demand** | 10 | ≥5 shops put money down (deposit/LOI) at ≥$40/seat | STOP |
| **G4 Defensible tech** | 8 | Task is NOT trivially zero-shot for GPT-5/Gemini; proprietary logic adds real accuracy | STOP or pivot to structured-logic layer |
| **G5 Incumbent stance** | 12 | Either incumbents show partner interest (Plan B) OR clearly won't ship this soon (Plan A runway) | reassess |

**All five must be green to release the build tranche.** Any single fail = stop and keep the money.

---

## 6. Delegation to keep it part-time

- **You build**: backend + CV/ML pipeline + evals (your strength, ~5–8 hrs/wk).
- **Domain partner (equity/rev-share)**: owns NFPA-25 correctness, labeled-photo supply, trade
  intros, and pilot recruiting — the non-delegable trust work you cannot do yourself.
- **Contractor (only post-gates)**: PWA/mobile UI; well-specced, fixed scope.
- **Honest caveat**: even fully delegated, the trust-based selling is NOT delegable and lands on you
  or the partner in evening hours — the same slot CutLog needs. This is the strongest structural
  reason to prefer Plan B (BD/license) if T2 shows any life.

**Plan B (feature-partnership)** is the lowest-time, highest-EV shape: you build a CV module, license
it to an incumbent, they bring data + distribution. It is a BD deal, not a company — which fits a
10–20 hr/wk secondary stream far better than a direct-sales grind into a conservative trade.

---

## 7. Cheapest validation before spending real money (summary)

**Spend ≤$5K and ~6–8 weeks of evenings before any hire or build.** In order:
1. Trial the incumbents; write down the real (small) gap. — $0
2. Land one credible domain partner (G1). — $0
3. 8–12 pain/WTP interviews (G2/G3). — $0
4. Zero-shot vision spike on real photos (G4) — plays to your strength. — ~$500
5. Landing page + mock + fake-door with paid LOIs (G3 hard proof). — ~$1.5–2.5K
6. Probe incumbent partner interest (G5/Plan B). — $0

If gates don't all pass — the likely outcome — you've spent ~$5K to definitively kill it and free
your scarce hours for CutLog or a higher-fit idea. **That is the intended, successful result of this
plan.**

---

## 8. Recommendation

**PASS / do not build as a startup.** If Hooman wants exposure to this space, pursue only **Plan B
(license a CV module to an incumbent)** and only after the ≤$5K validation confirms T1–T4. On the
honest scale this ranks below CutLog (4.5) and buy-a-micro-SaaS (5.2); its best realistic outcome
($0–2K/mo net base case) does not meet the $5–30K/mo goal.
